localContext: Hoffman Estates homes, especially those in Highlands, Winston Knolls, and Barrington Square, often feature garage doors from the 1960s-80s. These raised ranches and split-levels typically have attached two-car garages. Many still use original wood-composite doors. problemSigns.detail: This often means a torsion spring has snapped due to fatigue.

problemSigns.sign: Door won't lift or feels extremely heavy
problemSigns.detail: A broken spring removes the counterbalance, making the door weigh its full amount.

problemSigns.sign: Visible gap in the torsion spring above the door
problemSigns.detail: A clear separation in the spring coil confirms a break.

problemSigns.sign: Door lifts a few inches then stops
problemSigns.detail: This can happen when one of two extension springs breaks, creating an imbalance.
When a spring breaks, tension is lost, causing cables to hang loosely.
